001package org.krmdemo.techlabs.core.utils;
002
003import org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils;
004
005import java.util.Arrays;
006import java.util.List;
007import java.util.Map;
008import java.util.Objects;
009import java.util.function.Supplier;
010import java.util.stream.Collector;
011import java.util.stream.Collectors;
012import java.util.stream.Stream;
013
014import static org.krmdemo.techlabs.core.utils.CountingUtils.countingMap;
015
016/**
017 * Utility-class to work with strings, words and characters
018 * (some extension to JDK and {@link org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils})
019 */
020public class CoreStringUtils {
021
022    /**
023     * Quite the same as JDK's utility-method {@link Objects#requireNonNull(Object, String)},
024     * but in addition to valid non-{@code null} reference the passed string requires to be non-blank
025     * (contains at least one non-whitespace character)
026     *
027     * @param str a string (or any type that extends {@link CharSequence}) that requires to be non-blank
028     * @return the input string {@code str} if it's non-blank
029     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the input string {@code str} is blank
030     * @see StringUtils#isBlank(CharSequence)
031     */
032    public static <S extends CharSequence> S requiredNonBlank(S str) {
033        return requiredNonBlank(str, "input string must NOT be blank");
034    }
035
036    /**
037     * Quite the same as JDK's utility-method {@link Objects#requireNonNull(Object)},
038     * but in addition to valid non-{@code null} reference the passed string requires to be non-blank
039     * (contains at least one non-whitespace character)
040     *
041     * @param str a string (or any type that extends {@link CharSequence}) that requires to be non-blank
042     * @return the input string {@code str} if it's non-blank
043     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the input string {@code str} is blank
044     * @see StringUtils#isBlank(CharSequence)
045     */
046    public static <S extends CharSequence> S requiredNonBlank(S str, String errorMessage) {
047        return requiredNonBlank(str, () -> errorMessage);
048    }
049
050    /**
051     * Quite the same as JDK's utility-method {@link Objects#requireNonNull(Object, Supplier)},
052     * but in addition to valid non-{@code null} reference the passed string requires to be non-blank
053     * (contains at least one non-whitespace character)
054     *
055     * @param str a string (or any type that extends {@link CharSequence}) that requires to be non-blank
056     * @param errMsgSupplier a supplier for error message (to postpone the calculation if it's non-trivial)
057     * @return the input string {@code str} if it's non-blank
058     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the input string {@code str} is blank
059     * @param <S> any type that extends {@link CharSequence}
060     * @see StringUtils#isBlank(CharSequence)
061     */
062    public static <S extends CharSequence> S requiredNonBlank(S str, Supplier<String> errMsgSupplier) {
063        if (StringUtils.isBlank(str)) {
064            throw new IllegalArgumentException(errMsgSupplier.get());
065        }
066        return str;
067    }
068
069    /**
070     * Just a short-cut of JDK-invocation: <pre>{@code
071     *     Collectors.joining(System.lineSeparator())
072     * }</pre>
073     * @return the {@link Collector} that join the stream of strings with {@link System#lineSeparator()}
074     */
075    public static Collector<CharSequence, ?, String> multiLine() {
076        return Collectors.joining(System.lineSeparator());
077    }
078
079    /**
080     * @param str a string (eventually {@link CharSequence} to get the stream of chars
081     * @return the stream of chars as {@link Stream Stream&lt;Character&gt;}
082     */
083    public static Stream<Character> streamChars(CharSequence str) {
084        return str.chars().mapToObj(ch -> (char)ch);
085    }
086
087    /**
088     * Count the characters in passed string
089     *
090     * @param str a string to count the characters (as {@link CharSequence}
091     * @return a counting-map of characters in passed {@code str}
092     */
093    public static Map<Character, Integer> countingCharsMap(CharSequence str) {
094        return countingMap(streamChars(str));
095    }
096
097    /**
098     * Split the passed sentence on alphanumeric words
099     *
100     * @param sentence a string to sp[lit
101     * @return a {@link Stream Stream&lt;String&gt;} of alphanumeric words
102     */
103    public static Stream<String> splitWords(String sentence) {
104        return Arrays.stream(sentence.split("\\W"))
105            .map(String::trim)
106            .filter(word -> !word.isEmpty());
107    }
108
109    /**
110     * Split the passed sentence on alphanumeric words
111     *
112     * @param sentence a string to sp[lit
113     * @return a {@link List List&lt;String&gt;} of alphanumeric words
114     */
115    public static List<String> splitWordsList(String sentence) {
116        return splitWords(sentence).collect(Collectors.toList());
117    }
118
119    /**
120     * The same as {@link Collectors#joining(CharSequence)} with empty delimiter,
121     * but the elements of string are concatenated in <b>reversed order</b>.
122     * <hr/>
123     * <u><i>Note:</i></u> Not use for large streams, because  {@link StringBuilder#insert(int, Object)}
124     * is much slower than {@link StringBuilder#append(Object)} when the length of buffer is very big.
125     *
126     * @return the result as {@link CharSequence} (no extra copy of the result!)
127     * @param <T> the type of input elements to the reduction operation
128     */
129    public static <T> Collector<T, ?, CharSequence> joiningReversed() {
130        return joiningReversed("");
131    }
132
133    /**
134     * The same as {@link Collectors#joining(CharSequence)},
135     * but the elements of string are concatenated in <b>reversed order</b>.
136     * <hr/>
137     * <u><i>Note:</i></u> Not use for large streams, because  {@link StringBuilder#insert(int, Object)}
138     * is much slower than {@link StringBuilder#append(Object)} when the length of buffer is very big.
139     *
140     * @return the result as {@link CharSequence} (no extra copy of the result!)
141     * @param <T> the type of input elements to the reduction operation
142     */
143    public static <T> Collector<T, ?, CharSequence> joiningReversed(String delimiter) {
144        return joiningReversed(delimiter, "", "");
145    }
146
147    /**
148     * The same as {@link Collectors#joining(CharSequence, CharSequence, CharSequence)},
149     * but the elements of string are concatenated in <b>reversed order</b>.
150     * <hr/>
151     * <u><i>Note:</i></u> Not use for large streams, because  {@link StringBuilder#insert(int, Object)}
152     * is much slower than {@link StringBuilder#append(Object)} when the length of buffer is very big.
153     *
154     * @return the result as {@link CharSequence} (no extra copy of the result!)
155     * @param <T> the type of input elements to the reduction operation
156     */
157    public static <T> Collector<T, ?, CharSequence> joiningReversed(String delimiter, String prefix, String suffix) {
158        return Collector.of(
159            StringBuilder::new,
160            (sb, value) -> {
161                if (!sb.isEmpty() && !delimiter.isEmpty()) {
162                    sb.insert(0, delimiter);
163                }
164                sb.insert(0, value);
165            },
166            (left, right) -> { // the combiner is required for parallel streams
167                right.append(delimiter).append(left); return right;
168            },
169            sb -> sb.insert(0, prefix).append(suffix)
170        );
171    }
172
173    /**
174     * This method could be used to check whether the multi-line output ends with {@link System#lineSeparator() new-line}-symbol(s),
175     * because in most cases it's quite impossible to realize that fact visually (unless using different background).
176     * <hr/>
177     * TODO: introduce a method to detect extra white-spaces before new-line like {@code git-diff} is doing
178     *
179     * @param str the string to check
180     * @return {@code true} if the passed line is not empty, and it does not end with {@link System#lineSeparator() new-line}-symbol(s)
181     */
182    public static boolean hasNoNewLineAtTheEnd(String str) {
183        return StringUtils.isNotEmpty(str) && !str.endsWith(System.lineSeparator());
184    }
185
186    // --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
187
188    private CoreStringUtils() {
189        // prohibit the creation of utility-class instance
190        throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Cannot instantiate utility-class " + getClass().getName());
191    }
192}
